technology.title: Jayshree Ullal's Arista Just Posted 35% Growth. The AI Networking Boom Is Only Getting Started.
technology.excerpt: Arista Networks, led by Indian-origin CEO Jayshree Ullal, reported $2.71 billion in Q1 revenue and raised its AI networking target to $3.5 billion — but supply constraints in memory, optics, and wafers threaten to cap what could be an even bigger run.
technology.image_caption: Jayshree Ullal, CEO of Arista Networks (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Jayshree Ullal, born in London to Indian parents and raised in New Delhi, has turned Arista into a $194 billion company. For Indian network engineers and infrastructure architects across Silicon Valley, her company's AI-driven growth is creating a new wave of high-paying roles.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nadella Is Building Microsoft's Own AI Brain. The OpenAI Divorce Gets Real.
technology.excerpt: Microsoft will unveil homegrown coding, reasoning, and speech models at Build 2026 next week — its clearest signal yet that the $13 billion OpenAI partnership is becoming a backup plan, not the main one.
technology.image_caption: Satya Nadella, CEO of Microsoft (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Microsoft employs more Indian engineers on H-1B visas than almost any other company. If Nadella's in-house AI pivot reshapes product teams and hiring priorities, tens of thousands of Indian technologists in Redmond and the Bay Area will feel it first.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Dell's AI Revenue Explodes 757%. The Pentagon Just Handed It $9.7 Billion More.
technology.excerpt: The biggest earnings surprise of the AI era raises a question for every Indian engineer at Dell's Bangalore and Hyderabad campuses: how long before AI server demand reshapes their jobs too?
technology.nri_angle: Dell employs over 25,000 engineers across India in Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Chennai — its largest R&D footprint outside the US. As AI server revenue explodes, the skills demanded at these centers are shifting from traditional enterprise hardware to AI infrastructure, GPU orchestration, and liquid cooling systems. NRI investors who missed the Nvidia run should note Dell's stock is up 150% since February.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TSMC Is Raising Chip Prices 15%. Every AI Company Will Pay.
technology.excerpt: The world's most important chipmaker is finally leveraging its monopoly on advanced manufacturing — and the cost increases will ripple from Nvidia's data centers to India's semiconductor ambitions.
technology.nri_angle: Indian engineers at Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Marvell, and Qualcomm all design chips manufactured by TSMC. Price hikes directly affect their companies' margins and product roadmaps. India's own semiconductor mission — including the Tata Electronics fab in Dholera — relies heavily on TSMC-trained process engineers. And for NRI investors holding chip stocks, TSMC's pricing power is the single biggest variable in the sector's profitability calculus.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Atlassian's Indian-Origin CTO Is Out. His Replacement's Job Title Says Everything.
technology.excerpt: The Jira maker cut 1,600 jobs and replaced CTO Rajeev Rajan with AI-focused leaders — a restructuring that signals what's coming for senior Indian tech executives across Silicon Valley.
technology.nri_angle: Rajeev Rajan's departure is the highest-profile exit of an Indian-origin CTO in the current AI restructuring wave. Every Indian IT company and GCC in the world uses Atlassian's tools — Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket are the operating system of Indian software development. The 250 jobs cut in India directly affect H-1B holders and Indian engineers. And the broader signal — that AI expertise now trumps traditional engineering leadership — should concern every senior Indian tech executive whose resume emphasizes scale over AI.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TCS Shed 25,000 Jobs in Nine Months. It Also Doubled Its Fresher Intake.
technology.excerpt: India's largest IT employer is hollowing out its middle while flooding the bottom with AI-trained graduates — a workforce pyramid inversion that signals what's coming for the entire outsourcing industry.
technology.image_caption: Indian IT services companies are restructuring their workforces around AI, cutting experienced staff while doubling entry-level hiring.
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs with family at TCS, Infosys, or Wipro — and that's a lot of NRIs — these numbers are personal. For H-1B holders at Indian IT firms in the US, the restructuring raises questions about which onsite roles survive. And for diaspora investors, TCS's AI pivot is a test case for whether India's IT giants can transform without destroying their own value proposition.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Google's $15 Billion Vizag Bet Pits AI Ambition Against India's Water Crisis
technology.excerpt: The search giant's largest data center investment outside the US promises to transform a coastal Andhra Pradesh city — but farmers are being pushed off their land and rights groups warn the water math doesn't add up.
technology.image_caption: A modern data center server room — Google's Vizag facility will be India's first hub for training large-scale AI models.
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs from Andhra Pradesh, this is personal: your hometown is being remade to train the AI models you use at work in Mountain View. For diaspora investors, Google's India infrastructure bet could reshape the company's cost structure. And for anyone who sends money home, the water-vs-tech tradeoff playing out in Vizag previews a tension that will define India's next decade.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Is Claude's Second-Biggest Market. Every AI Lab Is Racing to Get In.
technology.excerpt: Anthropic's Bengaluru office, an Indian-origin co-creator behind the $2.5 billion Claude Code product, and 100 million weekly ChatGPT users — India has become the most contested AI consumer market outside America.
technology.image_caption: India has quietly become the world's second-largest market for AI coding tools, catching Silicon Valley's attention.
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers like Sid Bidasaria are building the AI tools that NRIs use daily — and the companies they work for are now racing to sell those tools back to India. For diaspora tech workers, this creates career opportunities on both sides of the Pacific. For NRI investors, India's emergence as a top-two AI consumer market signals a demand curve that hasn't been priced in.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Anushka Sharma Invested in Virat Kohli's Sportswear Company. Now She's Building a Yoga Line Under His Brand.
entertainment.excerpt: The actress picked up a minority stake in Agilitas Sports and will co-develop One8 Yoga — launching on International Yoga Day, June 21. Her last film was six years ago.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Salman Khan Screened Maatrubhumi for Bollywood's Biggest Directors. Subhash Ghai Called It a 'Must-Watch.'
entertainment.excerpt: Sooraj Barjatya, Kabir Khan, David Dhawan, and Riteish Deshmukh watched the rough cut of the Galwan Valley-inspired war drama. A release date still hasn't been announced.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Mammootty and Mohanlal's Patriot Hits ZEE5 on June 5. It Cost ₹140 Crore. The Theatres Couldn't Save It.
entertainment.excerpt: Malayalam cinema's most anticipated reunion in two decades underperformed at the box office. Now NRIs who missed it get a second chance — in five languages.

entertainment.excerpt: Puja Entertainment claims Tips Industries used iconic 'Chunari Chunari' and 'Ishq Sona Hai' from Biwi No.1 without permission. The Bombay High Court hearing could decide if Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai opens on June 5.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Aamir Khan's Sitaare Zameen Par Premieres on TV This Saturday. It Made ₹268 Crore. Most NRIs Haven't Seen It.
entertainment.excerpt: The basketball comedy-drama — a spiritual sequel to Taare Zameen Par — hits Sony MAX on May 31, bringing Aamir's quietest box office success to living rooms across India and the diaspora.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Suriya's Karuppu Just Crossed ₹270 Crore Worldwide. He Waited 13 Years for a Hit This Big.
entertainment.excerpt: The Tamil fantasy drama shattered Singam 2's lifetime in four days, became Suriya's biggest film in Kerala, and reunited him with Trisha after 21 years.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal Brought Their Baby to the Airport. They Asked Photographers to Put Their Cameras Down.
entertainment.excerpt: Seven months after welcoming son Vihaan, the couple introduced him to Mumbai's paparazzi — with one firm condition attached.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Bhooth Bangla Is Still Running in Theatres After Six Weeks. Akshay Kumar Hasn't Done That in Years.
entertainment.excerpt: The Akshay Kumar–Priyadarshan reunion has crossed ₹176 crore in India and ₹262 crore worldwide, defying the fast-exit box office cycle.
entertainment.image_caption: Akshay Kumar's horror-comedy Bhooth Bangla has become his strongest post-pandemic performer
entertainment.nri_angle: Bhooth Bangla earned over ₹56 crore overseas — one of Akshay's strongest international runs in years, driven by NRI families nostalgic for the Kumar-Priyadarshan comedy formula.

entertainment.title: India's Largest Cinema Chain Just Launched a Pride Film Festival. The Lineup Includes a Marathi Film.
entertainment.excerpt: PVR INOX is screening Moonlight, Rocketman, and the celebrated Baapya across 20 cities and 40 cinemas, starting May 29.
entertainment.image_caption: PVR INOX's Pride Film Festival celebrates queer cinema across 20 Indian cities
entertainment.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up before Section 377 was struck down, seeing India's largest cinema chain program a Pride film festival signals institutional acceptance at mainstream scale.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Karan Johar Unfollowed Shah Rukh Khan, Alia Bhatt, and Nearly Everyone Else on Instagram. He Called It a Digital Detox.
entertainment.excerpt: The filmmaker kept only one Bollywood name on his following list — Priyanka Chopra — and told the internet to stop making it 'national news.'
entertainment.image_caption: Social media detox has become a recurring theme among Bollywood celebrities
entertainment.nri_angle: The Karan Johar–Shah Rukh Khan friendship is foundational mythology for NRIs — their films defined an entire generation's relationship with Indian identity abroad.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Netflix Put Dubai's Richest Indians on Camera. The Internet Can't Decide Whether to Cringe or Binge.
entertainment.excerpt: Desi Bling premiered with a viral on-screen engagement, Bollywood cameos, and enough drama to make Dubai Bling look subtle. It's already on Netflix's global charts.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Genetic Variant Carried by 1 in 13 South Asians Makes the Standard Diabetes Blood Test Unreliable. Researchers Say Thousands of Cases Are Being Missed.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Two separate studies have found that common genetic variants in South Asian and Black populations artificially lower HbA1c results — the test your doctor uses to diagnose and monitor diabetes. The implications for the Indian diaspora are enormous.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Wildfire Smoke Does Not Just Burn Your Lungs. A Growing Body of Research Says It Is Rewiring Your Brain.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Dementia risk, cognitive decline, and mental illness in children — the neuroscience of wildfire smoke is catching up to what California residents already sense. Indian-Americans in the Bay Area and LA are disproportionately exposed.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Wildfire smoke over a city skyline — fine particulate matter from these events can cross the blood-brain barrier and trigger neuroinflammation.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Trial of 410 Cancer Survivors Found That Four Weeks of Gentle Yoga Reduced Insomnia, Fatigue, and Anxiety. No Medication Required.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The YOCAS programme, presented at ASCO 2026, is built on hatha and restorative yoga — practices that Indian families have known for generations. Western oncology is finally catching up.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A gentle yoga session — the kind of hatha and restorative practice now shown to significantly reduce insomnia and fatigue in cancer survivors.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 39,000 Women Found That Two Hours of Brisk Walking Per Week Cuts Stroke Risk by 30 Per Cent. Running Did Not Do Better.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Women's Health Study tracked participants for twelve years. Brisk walking outperformed vigorous exercise for stroke prevention. South Asian women in the US have among the lowest physical activity rates of any demographic group.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study Found That Coffee Reshapes Your Gut Bacteria and Improves Your Mood. Caffeine Had Nothing to Do With It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Nature Communications trial separated 62 adults into coffee drinkers and non-drinkers, then removed coffee for two weeks. When it came back — caffeinated or decaf — stress and depression scores dropped in both groups. The gut-brain axis, not the caffeine, was doing the work.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Review of Every Major Vaping Study Since 2017 Found DNA Damage, Heavy Metals, and Early Cancer Signals. 'Safer Than Cigarettes' Was Never the Same as 'Safe.'
lifestyle-health.excerpt: E-cigarette aerosols contain formaldehyde, nickel, and chromium. Asian-American teens are among the fastest-growing users. Indian-American parents may be the last to notice.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: E-cigarette aerosols contain DNA-damaging compounds including formaldehyde and heavy metals.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Yale Study of 540,000 People Found That Your Body Can Tell the Difference Between Working Hard and Working Out. Only One of Them Protects Your Health.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: New research in Nature Genetics shows leisure-time exercise activates biological pathways that workplace movement and household chores simply cannot replicate. Indian-American professionals are among the most affected.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Leisure-time exercise — the kind you choose to do — activates biological pathways that workplace movement cannot replicate.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India's Largest State Just Launched a Wellness Policy to Turn Varanasi and Ayodhya Into Global Ayurveda Hubs. Your Next Trip Home Could Include a Panchakarma Prescription.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Uttar Pradesh's AYUSH Health and Wellness Policy 2026 is India's most ambitious bet on wellness tourism yet. For NRIs spending $3,000 on a weekend spa in Sedona, the same money in Varanasi will get you a month of traditional medicine with a lineage older than Western civilisation.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 463,000 People Found That Loneliness Raises Your Risk of Heart Valve Disease by 23 Per Cent. Living Alone Does Not. The Distinction Matters More Than You Think.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The largest study of its kind found that feeling lonely — not being socially isolated — independently predicts degenerative valve disease. For a diaspora that prizes stoicism and treats loneliness as weakness, the findings are a clinical alarm bell.

sources.label: Journal of the American Heart Association

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: European Cardiologists Now Say Ultra-Processed Food Is a Clinical Risk Factor — Like Smoking. Indian-Americans Eat More of It Every Year They Live Here.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A European Society of Cardiology consensus links UPFs to 65 per cent higher cardiovascular mortality. The traditional Indian kitchen was always the answer.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: The traditional Indian kitchen — dal, sabzi, whole spices — is inherently minimally processed. European cardiologists now say that matters more than calorie counts.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India Just Quarantined a Suspected Ebola Patient in Bengaluru. The US and Canada Have Banned Travellers From Three African Countries. Here Is What Every NRI Needs to Know.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The WHO has declared a global health emergency. India has launched airport screening. If you have family travelling between India and East Africa, the rules changed overnight.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Airport health screening measures have been activated across India and dozens of other countries in response to the Ebola outbreak
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Blood Test Can Now Screen You for Colon Cancer. The American Cancer Society Just Made It Official. South Asian Americans Have the Lowest Screening Rates in the Country.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Guardant Shield test detects tumour DNA in your blood. One in three eligible Americans remain unscreened. For South Asians, that number may be three in four.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A simple blood draw can now screen for colorectal cancer under updated ACS guidelines. | Pexels
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.excerpt: New Delhi has told state-run fuel companies to build LPG storage for a full month of national demand — a direct response to the Strait of Hormuz crisis that has already choked India's basmati exports and driven up global energy prices.
carousel.nri_angle: Energy security is the thread connecting kitchen budgets in Lucknow to remittance values in New Jersey. When LPG prices spike, the rupee weakens, inflation rises, and the purchasing power of dollar-denominated NRI remittances shifts.

carousel.excerpt: A four-game sweep of Cleveland. An eleven-game winning streak. And for the millions of NRIs in the tri-state area, a summer with the Finals and the World Cup in the same city.
carousel.image_caption: The New York Knicks swept the Cavaliers to reach the NBA Finals for the first time in 27 years.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Meta Wants You to Pay for WhatsApp. Here's What That Means for 500 Million Indians.
carousel.excerpt: Facebook Plus, Instagram Plus, and WhatsApp Plus subscriptions are rolling out globally. India pricing is still TBD — but the diaspora's most essential app just entered the subscription era.
carousel.image_caption: Meta's subscription push spans Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp — apps used by hundreds of millions of Indians daily.
carousel.nri_angle: WhatsApp is the connective tissue of the Indian diaspora — the family group chat, the money transfer coordination, the NRI grapevine. Any monetization move by Meta here touches every Indian abroad personally. Creator and business tiers also reshape the economics for India's massive influencer and SMB ecosystem.
